apiUrl.description: Base URL of the Atlas Backend API. Defaults to `https://api.atlasauth.net`, or the `ATLAS_API_URL` environment variable when set.

platformKey.description: Atlas platform key (`psk_...`), needed only by platform resources such as `atlas.IdApp` (Sign in with Atlas apps). Prefer the `ATLAS_PLATFORM_KEY` environment variable.

secretKey.description: Atlas instance secret key (`sk_...`). Prefer the `ATLAS_SECRET_KEY` environment variable so the key never lands in state or config.

attributes.description: — Extra HTML attributes your CMP's click handler listens for. Allowed names: `data-*`, `aria-*`, `id`, `class` and `href` (an https URL or a `#fragment`), lower case; at most 10, values up to 200 characters. `data-atlas-*` and event handlers (`on*`) are refused. Set a `preset`, `attributes`, or both.

label.description: — The link text, 1–60 characters, e.g. `Cookie settings`.

preset.description: — The CMP's reopen trigger: `cookiemunch` (adds `data-cc="show-settings"`), `cookiebot` (calls `Cookiebot.renew()`), `onetrust` (calls `OneTrust.ToggleInfoDisplay()`) or `custom` (adds nothing; use `attributes`).

renderedAttributes.description: — What Atlas renders on the link: `attributes` with the preset's trigger applied.

active.description: — Whether the plan is offered. Defaults to `true`.

amount.description: — A free-form display string for the price, stored verbatim by Atlas — not parsed or converted. Use whatever units you display (e.g. `12.00` for $12, or `1200` for cents); Atlas does not interpret it. Pair it with `currency` and `interval`.

audience.description: — Who may subscribe: `user` or `org`. Defaults to `user`.

currency.description: — ISO currency code (e.g. `usd`). Defaults to `usd`.

features.description: — Feature keys this plan grants, surfaced as the `fea` session claim.

free.description: — True when the plan has no `stripePriceId`.

interval.description: — Billing interval: `month` or `year`. Defaults to `month`.

limits.description: — Numeric caps the plan grants, keyed by limit name (e.g. `{ maxSeats = 25, maxDevices = 5 }`). Where `features` answer "can they?", limits answer "how many?"; they are surfaced on the verified token and merged under any per-organization override. Unset keeps the plan's current limits (none for a new plan); `{}` clears them.

trialDays.description: — Free trial length in days (0–3650), or omitted for none.

allowedOrigins.description:
— Exact origins (`scheme://host[:port]`, no
wildcards, no path) permitted for the widget / JS SDK and OAuth redirect
validation. Native-app webview origins (`tauri://`, `capacitor://`,
`ionic://`) are accepted.

authConfig.description: — The instance auth configuration as a JSON object string (use `jsonencode(...)`). A partial patch merged into the current config server-side. State holds exactly the patch you wrote (round-tripped verbatim), not the server-merged object, so a partial patch does not thrash the plan. The full effective configuration is exposed separately as `authConfigResolved`.

authConfigResolved.description: The full effective configuration Atlas resolved from your `authConfig` plus defaults (read-only).

environment.description: The instance environment (e.g. `production`, `development`).

frontendApiHost.description: The instance Frontend API host (read-only; auto-assigned by Atlas).

nativeApps.description: — Typed native-app passkey association, folded into the `authConfig` patch under `nativeApps` before it is sent (so you configure it with typed HCL instead of raw JSON). A value here **takes precedence** over any `nativeApps` embedded in the raw `authConfig` JSON. Atlas serves the matching `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` and `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` on the instance Frontend API host (`frontendApiHost`). atlas:index/getInstancePreflight:getInst.description: ## # atlas.getInstancePreflight (Data Source) Checks your instance setup in one call and lists everything Atlas can see is broken or worth knowing: social providers enabled without credentials, OAuth clients that cannot complete a sign-in, custom domains not serving yet, email sign-in with no email provider, and more. Each finding says what is wrong and how to fix it. Use it with a `check` block (a warning on every plan) or a `precondition` (fail the plan) to catch setup mistakes before they reach users. API: `GET /v1/instance/preflight`.

outputs.description: A collection of values returned by getInstancePreflight.

findings.description:
— Ordered error, then warning, then info. (see
below for nested schema)

id.description: — Always `preflight`.

ok.description: — True when there are no error-severity findings.
